test_title: PYST 15: SSC GD Constable - English (Held on: 24th November 2021 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Suddenly, it started raining and I _______ an umbrella from the office.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Borrowed**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Borrow** means taking and using something belonging to someone else with the intention of returning it.

 
 
• **Example -** *He had **borrowed** a car from one of his colleagues.*
 
 
 
• So, it is clear that the most appropriate word is **'borrowed'.**
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Criticise** means indicating the faults of someone or something in a disapproving way.
 
• **Lend** means grant to someone the use of something on the understanding that it will be returned.
 
• **Substitute** means a person or thing acting or serving in place of another.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• Borrow and Lend - These two verbs cause a great amount of confusion!
 
• **Borrow is a regular verb** meaning **'get something from someone, intending to give it back after a short time'. **
 
 
• **Example **- Could I **borrow **your pen for a minute, please?
 
 
 
• **Lend** means **‘give something to someone for a short time, expecting that you will get it back’.** The past simple and the -ed form are lent.
 
 
• **Example -*** I never **lend** my books to anyone.*
